newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Northrop deal lights up market.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Northrop deal lights up market.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp set off rockets in the U.S. corporate bond market with its announcement on Thursday that it planned to acquire Northrop Grumman Corp in a $11.6 billion stock transaction, traders said.
Northrop debt (Baa3/BBB-minus) of various maturities shot up 15 basis points to 20 basis points on the news, fueled by speculation that the merger would spark a ratings upgrade.
Prices on Lockheed debt A3/BBB-plus) was unchanged, traders said, despite views by some analysts that its ratings could be weakened.

In other news, prices of IXC Communications Inc junk bonds slumped after the company announced on Thursday that it expects earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) for the second quarter and the year to be below its previous estimates.
The long-distance telephone company's 12.5 percent senior notes due '05 dropped two points on the news, one trader said.
In broader markets, junk bonds lagged rallying Treasury bonds, while their investment-grade counterparts simply echoed their gains, traders said.
Most junk bonds closed 3/8 to 1/2 a point higher, while investment-grade corporate bond spreads were unchanged to slighlty tighter, traders said.

Meanwhile, the June U.S. employment report portraying moderate job growth and the near abscence of wage inflation sent the prices of the 30-year Treasury up 1-11/32 to 100-8/32. Some profit taking cut these gains to 100-1/32 toward the end of the day.
Two junk bond new issues represented the bulk of the action in the corproate bond primary market on Thursday.
